info.title: Iriks-IT API
info.description:
The official API for [Iriks-IT](https://iriks-it.nl). Powering tools, collections, and mischief since Sam knocked the first server off the desk.

> *"Why did Sam write the API docs? Because Silvia said if he didn't, she'd replace him with a 404 page."*

All authenticated endpoints require a Bearer token obtained via `/auth/login`. Tokens expire after **24 hours** — roughly the time it takes Silvia to forgive you for waking her up.

servers.description: Production — where Sam and Silvia live

tags.name: account
tags.description: Purr-fectly secure account management. Sam and Silvia got in, so can you. Email verification required — no exceptions, not even for cats.

tags.name: hotwheels
tags.description: Hot Wheels collection tracker. Silvia tried to bat a few under the sofa, but every car is accounted for.

tags.name: tools
tags.description: Utility endpoints for IP intelligence. Sam sniffs every packet — you get a nice JSON response instead.

tags.name: webhooks
tags.description: Inbound webhook receivers. Silvia sits on the server and intercepts every status update — nothing gets past her.

tags.name: vrchat
tags.description: VRChat member lookups and group membership data. Silvia runs the door policy — Sam checks the ban list.

tags.name: vrchat-moderation
tags.description: Moderation actions: kick, ban, and ban appeals. Neither Silvia nor Sam tolerates rule-breakers.

tags.name: vrchat-member-data
tags.description: Per-member moderator records: notes and warnings. Sam has more warnings than notes. We don't talk about it.

tags.name: vrchat-content
tags.description: Group content creation: posts and calendar events. Silvia approves all posts before Sam hits send.

tags.name: vrchat-images
tags.description: VRChat group media gallery management. Images are scoped to a group's Media Uploads gallery, created automatically on first use. Upload, list, inspect, and remove images per group. Reference the `image_id` when creating posts. Sam once uploaded 47 cat photos before Silvia noticed the gallery existed.

tags.name: incidents
tags.description: Historic incident log from Atlassian statuspage and Cronitor monitoring sources. Independent of notification providers — whether or not Silvia triggered a Discord alert, every incident lands here.

tags.name: vulnerabilities
tags.description: GitHub security vulnerability tracking. Silvia audits every dependency. Sam pretends he doesn't see the alerts. The truth is here regardless.

tags.name: rdw
tags.description: Dutch vehicle (kenteken) lookups via the RDW open data API. Silvia once parked in a no-parking zone — Sam checked the RDW data and confirmed it was definitely her car.

tags.name: fun
tags.description: Endpoints that exist purely because they're funny. Silvia and Sam approved this entire tag; no further oversight was requested.

post.description: Register your account here. You will receive a verification email — check your inbox, not your spam (or your cat's food bowl). You must verify before you can log in.

200.description: Account registered successfully. Check your email to verify.

example.data: Account already exists, please choose a different one.

post.description: You found the verification code in your email — now submit it here to unlock API access. Unlike Sam, who needs zero verification to knock things off tables.

200.description: Account verified. You may now log in.

409.description: Verification failed — invalid or expired code.

example.data: Something bad broke, please contact: api@iriks-it.nl

post.summary: Log in and obtain a Bearer token
post.description: Exchange your credentials for an access token and a refresh token. The access token expires after 24 hours — about the same time Sam takes to forgive you for closing the bedroom door. The refresh token is valid for 30 days and can be exchanged at `/auth/refresh` for a fresh pair. You must have verified your account first.

200.description: Login successful. Use `token` as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on all protected endpoints. Store `refresh_token` securely — Sam guards his with his life.

403.description: Account not verified yet — Silvia is still screening you.

example.data: Account hasn't been verified yet, please verify this first!

post.description:
Exchange a valid refresh token for a fresh access token + refresh token pair. The old refresh token is immediately invalidated — single-use, like Sam's patience when his food bowl is empty.

Send the refresh token (not the access token) in the `Authorization: Bearer` header. Using an access token here will be rejected with 403.

200.description: New token pair issued. The old refresh token is now dead — Silvia shredded it.

401.description: The refresh token was not found — it may have already been used or expired. Sam says no.

403.description: The token provided does not have the `token-refresh` ability. You likely sent an access token instead of a refresh token — Silvia can tell the difference.

get.description: Returns the full Hot Wheels collection. Silvia once batted a 1970 Dodge Charger under the sofa. It was recovered. It is in this list.

200.description: Hot Wheels retrieved successfully.

data.detail: Sam sat on the box once but it survived. Purr-fect condition.
Silvia batted it off the shelf exactly once. We consider it loved.

200.description: Car added to the collection successfully.

200.description: Car retrieved successfully.

put.description: Update a car's name or detail. Silvia approved this endpoint with a slow blink.

200.description: Car updated successfully.

delete.description: Remove a car from the collection. More permanent than Silvia hiding it under the fridge.

200.description: Car deleted from the collection.

get.description:
Returns geolocation, ASN, proxy detection, and AbuseIPDB threat intelligence for an IPv4 or IPv6 address. Sam sniffs every packet — you get structured JSON.

Requires the `ip.lookup` permission scope on your token.

**Caching:** AbuseIPDB results are cached for 14 days per IP to stay well within rate limits. Fresh data is fetched automatically when the cache expires.

parameters.name: ip
parameters.description: The IPv4 or IPv6 address to look up. Sam's current IP is classified.

200.description: IP data retrieved successfully. Sam sniffed it and found no suspicious treats.

reports.comment: Sam detected suspicious SSH traffic from this IP at 3 AM. He woke up the admin by sitting on the keyboard.
Silvia noticed this IP sniffing her ports. She hissed at it and reported it immediately.

403.description: Missing `ip.lookup` permission scope on your token.

example.message: You do not have permission to perform IP lookups.

422.description: The provided value is not a valid IP address. Even Sam knows `meow` is not an IP.

example.message: The provided value is not a valid IP address.

post.summary: Report an IP address to AbuseIPDB
post.description:
Reports an IP address to AbuseIPDB under one or more category IDs. Sam keeps a personal logbook of every report filed under his watch — every request is recorded in our own history, sent or not.

Requires the `ip.report` permission scope on your token.

**Throttling:** the same IP address can only be reported once every 12 hours. AbuseIPDB itself only enforces a 15-minute minimum between reports for the same address, but Silvia prefers to let sleeping IPs lie a little longer before reporting them again. Reporting an IP within the window returns `429` with the last known score and the time the next report will be allowed.

parameters.name: ip
parameters.description: The IPv4 or IPv6 address to report. Sam double-checks it's not his own.

categories.description: AbuseIPDB category IDs (e.g. 18 = Brute-Force, 22 = SSH). See https://www.abuseipdb.com/categories for the full list.

comment.description: Optional details about the abuse (logs, ports, etc.). Sam appreciates specifics.
comment.example: Sam caught this IP trying every password on the SSH port at 3 AM.

200.description: Report submitted to AbuseIPDB successfully.

message.example: IP address reported to AbuseIPDB successfully.

example.message: IP address reported to AbuseIPDB successfully.

403.description: Missing `ip.report` permission scope on your token.

example.message: You do not have permission to report IP addresses.

422.description: Validation failed — invalid IP address, missing categories, or an unrecognised category ID. Even Sam knows category 9999 doesn't exist.

categories: The categories field must have at least 1 items.

429.description: This IP address was already reported within the last 12 hours. Silvia is making it wait its turn.

example.message: This IP address was already reported within the last 12 hours, so it wasn't sent to AbuseIPDB again.

502.description: AbuseIPDB rejected the report or no API key was available. Sam blames the WiFi.

example.message: Unable to submit the report to AbuseIPDB right now.

post.description:
Submit a ban appeal for a VRChat group ban. Requires a valid Bearer token with the `vrchat.banappeal` permission scope.

**Rate limit:** One appeal per IP address per 14 days. Silvia keeps count. Your IP address is recorded with the appeal.

> *"Sam submitted an appeal for knocking the server over. His reason: 'it looked unstable.' It was not accepted."*

vrchat_user_id.description: Your VRChat user ID. Must match `usr_<uuid>` format.

group_id.description: The VRChat group ID you were banned from. Must match `grp_<id>` format. Silvia checks every letter.

reason.description: Why you believe the ban should be lifted. Sam reads every word.
reason.example: I knocked that toy off the shelf on purpose, not by accident. I deserve to come back.

200.description: Appeal submitted. Silvia will review it when she wakes up from her nap.

message.example: Your ban appeal has been submitted.

example.message: Your ban appeal has been submitted.

403.description: Missing `vrchat.banappeal` permission scope on your token.

example.message: You do not have permission to submit VRChat ban appeals.

422.description: Validation failed. Check your field values — Sam flagged them.

vrchat_user_id: The vrchat user id field format is invalid.
email: The email field must be a valid email address.

429.description: An appeal from this IP was already submitted in the last 14 days. Silvia is still deliberating.

example.message: A ban appeal from this IP address was already submitted recently. Please wait 14 days before trying again.

get.summary: Look up whether a VRChat user is banned
get.description:
Checks the group's audit log history to determine whether a given VRChat user ID has ever been banned. Returns `banned: false` if no ban event is found. If banned, returns the actor, timestamp, description, and any operator notes.

Requires the `vrchat.banlookup` permission scope on your token.

> *"Sam sat on the ban list once and accidentally approved it. We added a notes field so we could write 'Sam did it again'."*

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: The VRChat user ID to look up. Must match the format `usr_<uuid>`. Silvia refuses to check anything else.

parameters.name: group_id
parameters.description: The VRChat group ID to scope the ban check to. Must match `grp_<id>` format.

200.description: Lookup completed. `banned: false` means the user is clean — for now. Silvia is watching.

reason.example: Knocked every cat toy out of the group instance.

notes.example: Third offence. Sam reviewed the footage. Unanimous decision.

data.reason: Knocked every cat toy out of the group instance.
data.notes: Third offence. Sam reviewed the footage. Unanimous decision.

403.description: Missing `vrchat.banlookup` permission scope on your token. Sam says no.

example.message: You do not have permission to perform VRChat ban lookups.

422.description: The provided value is not a valid VRChat user ID. Silvia only accepts `usr_<uuid>` format — she has standards.

example.message: The provided value is not a valid VRChat user ID.

get.summary: Look up a VRChat user by ID
get.description:
Fetches public profile information for a VRChat user directly from the VRChat API. Returns a curated set of public fields — location, friend status, login timestamps, and other private fields are intentionally omitted.

Requires the `vrchat.lookup` permission scope on your token.

> *"Silvia personally reviews every lookup. Sam just checks if it's his own ID so he can update his bio to 'not guilty'."*

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: The VRChat user ID to look up. Must match the format `usr_<uuid>`. Silvia only accepts valid IDs — she has standards.

parameters.name: group_id
parameters.description: The VRChat group ID to scope the lookup to. Must match `grp_<id>` format. Used to enrich the response with the member's group status.

200.description: User found. Silvia approves. Sam is jealous of the bio.

group_membership.description: The user's current membership record for the requested group, or `null` if they have no history there.

group_note.description: A moderator note about this member within the requested group, or `null` if no note has been written. Sam's note probably says 'watch the shelves'.

note.example: Silvia tends to knock things off shelves during events. Keep her away from the merch table.

moderator_name.description: Display name of the moderator who wrote the note.

group_warnings.description: List of warnings issued to this member within the requested group, ordered oldest-first. Empty array if none. (Silvia has two. They're both shelf-related.)

description.example: Pushed three mugs off the table during the cat café event.

moderator_name.description: Display name of the moderator who issued the warning.

reputation.description: Reputation counters for this user within the requested group. All fields default to `0` if no reputation record exists. Sam has a suspiciously high `instance_kicks` count.

instance_warns.description: Number of times the user has been warned in a group instance.

instance_kicks.description: Number of times the user has been kicked from a group instance.

group_joins.description: Number of times the user has joined the group.

group_leaves.description: Number of times the user has left the group.

group_kicks.description: Number of times the user has been kicked from the group.

group_bans.description: Number of times the user has been banned from the group.

group_note.note: Silvia tends to knock things off shelves during events. Keep her away from the merch table.

group_warnings.title: Shelf Incident #1
group_warnings.description: Pushed three mugs off the table during the cat café event.

403.description: Missing `vrchat.lookup` permission scope on your token. Silvia personally enforces this.

example.message: You do not have permission to perform VRChat user lookups.

404.description: VRChat user not found or the VRChat API returned no data. Sam checked twice — they're not there.

422.description: The provided value is not a valid VRChat user ID. Must match `usr_<uuid>`. Silvia only accepts valid IDs — she has standards.

example.message: The provided value is not a valid VRChat user ID.

get.description:
Returns all members in the specified VRChat group from the local sync database, enriched with their reputation tallies. Results are sorted alphabetically by display name.

Requires the `vrchat.members` permission scope on your token.

> *"Silvia compiled the member list. Sam reviewed it. Sam was on the list. Sam did not appreciate his own stats."*

parameters.name: group_id
parameters.description: VRChat group ID. Must match `grp_<id>`.

200.description: Member list retrieved.

403.description: Missing `vrchat.members` permission scope.

422.description: Missing or invalid group_id.

post.summary: Create or update a moderator note for a member
post.description:
Creates or replaces the moderator note for the given member within the specified group. There is exactly one note per member per group — calling this endpoint again overwrites the previous note and updates `updated_at`.

Requires the `vrchat.note` permission scope on your token.

> *"Silvia wrote the first note. It just said 'watched'. Sam's note has three paragraphs about the shelf incident."*

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: VRChat user ID (`usr_` prefix).

note.example: Tends to knock things off shelves during events. Keep her away from the merch table.

moderator_name.description: Display name of the moderator writing the note.

200.description: Note saved (created or updated).

data.note: Tends to knock things off shelves during events. Keep her away from the merch table.

403.description: Missing `vrchat.note` permission scope.

422.description: Validation error — invalid user ID format, missing or invalid group_id, empty note or moderator name.

delete.summary: Delete the moderator note for a member
delete.description:
Permanently removes the moderator note for the given member in the specified group. Requires `group_id` as a query parameter.

Requires the `vrchat.note` permission scope on your token.

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: VRChat user ID (`usr_` prefix).

parameters.name: group_id
parameters.description: VRChat group ID (`grp_` prefix).

200.description: Note deleted.

403.description: Missing `vrchat.note` permission scope.

422.description: Invalid user ID format or missing/invalid group_id.

post.summary: Add a warning to a member
post.description:
Appends a new warning record for the given member within the specified group. Members can accumulate multiple warnings — each call creates a new entry.

Requires the `vrchat.warning` permission scope on your token.

> *"Sam has issued one warning. Silvia has issued seventeen. We don't talk about the great shelf incident of 2026."*

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: VRChat user ID (`usr_` prefix).

description.example: Pushed three mugs off the table during the cat café event.

moderator_name.description: Display name of the moderator issuing the warning.

200.description: Warning created.

data.title: Shelf Incident #1
data.description: Pushed three mugs off the table during the cat café event.

403.description: Missing `vrchat.warning` permission scope.

422.description: Validation error — invalid user ID format, missing or invalid group_id, empty title, description, or moderator name.

post.summary: Kick a member from the group
post.description:
Removes a member from the VRChat group using the server's authenticated VRChat account. The account must hold the **Remove Group Members** permission in the group. A kicked member can rejoin if the group is open.

Requires the `vrchat.kick` permission scope on your token.

> *"Sam wrote the kick logic. Silvia reviewed it. She added an extra validation layer and a strongly-worded comment."*

user_id.description: VRChat user ID to kick. Must match `usr_<uuid>`.

200.description: Member kicked. Silvia watched from the doorstep.

403.description: Missing `vrchat.kick` scope or the VRChat account lacks the Remove Group Members permission.

422.description: Validation failed.

500.description: VRChat API failed to kick the member.

post.summary: Ban a member from the group
post.description:
Bans a user from the VRChat group using the server's authenticated VRChat account. The account must have group ban permissions. A banned user cannot rejoin and will appear in the group's ban list.

Requires the `vrchat.ban` permission scope on your token.

> *"Silvia personally reviews all ban requests. Sam types them in. Neither of them feels bad about it."*

user_id.description: VRChat user ID to ban. Must match `usr_<uuid>`.

200.description: Member banned. Silvia has updated her mental blocklist.

403.description: Missing `vrchat.ban` scope or the VRChat account lacks group ban permissions.

422.description: Validation failed.

500.description: VRChat API failed to ban the member.

get.summary: List images in the group media gallery
get.description:
Returns a paginated list of images from the group's Media Uploads gallery. The gallery is resolved (or created) automatically.

Requires the `vrchat.post` permission scope.

> *"Silvia reviewed the gallery. Sam had named every file 'cat.png'. There were 47 of them."*

parameters.name: group_id
parameters.description: VRChat group ID whose Media Uploads gallery to list.

parameters.name: n
parameters.description: Number of results to return (1-100, default 50).

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Pagination offset.

200.description: List of gallery images.

403.description: Missing `vrchat.post` permission scope, or the VRChat account cannot access the gallery.

422.description: `group_id` is missing.

500.description: Gallery could not be resolved or the VRChat API returned an error.

post.summary: Upload an image to the group media gallery
post.description:
Uploads a PNG or JPEG image to VRChat and adds it to the group's Media Uploads gallery (created automatically if it doesn't exist yet). Returns both the `image_id` for use in posts and the `gallery_image_id` needed to delete the image later.

Requires the `vrchat.post` permission scope on your token.

> *"Silvia submitted a photo of herself on the merch table. Sam uploaded it as the group banner. The gallery auto-created itself. We have no regrets."*

group_id.description: VRChat group ID to upload the image into.

file.description: PNG or JPEG image, max 10 MB.

200.description: Image uploaded and added to the group gallery. Use `image_id` in `POST /vrchat/posts`. Store `gallery_image_id` to delete the image later.

403.description: Missing `vrchat.post` permission scope, or the VRChat account cannot upload files or manage the gallery.

422.description: `group_id` missing, no file provided, wrong MIME type, or file exceeds 10 MB.

500.description: VRChat API failed to accept the upload, resolve the gallery, or add the image to the gallery.

get.description:
Returns details for a specific uploaded image by its `file_xxx` ID.

Requires the `vrchat.post` permission scope.

parameters.name: fileId
parameters.description: VRChat file ID (`file_` prefix).

200.description: File details.

403.description: Missing `vrchat.post` permission scope.

422.description: Invalid file ID format.

delete.summary: Remove an image from the group gallery and delete the file
delete.description:
Removes the image from the group's Media Uploads gallery and permanently deletes the underlying VRChat file. Both the `group_id` and the `gallery_image_id` (returned by `POST /vrchat/image`) are required. Make sure no posts are still referencing the image before deleting.

Requires the `vrchat.post` permission scope.

> *"Sam deleted the wrong image. Silvia had three back-ups. Sam did not. The gallery still remembers."*

parameters.name: fileId
parameters.description: VRChat file ID (`file_` prefix).

parameters.name: group_id
parameters.description: VRChat group ID the image belongs to.

parameters.name: gallery_image_id
parameters.description: Gallery image ID (`gimg_` prefix) returned by `POST /vrchat/image` or `GET /vrchat/images`.

200.description: Image removed from gallery and file deleted.

403.description: Missing `vrchat.post` permission scope, or the VRChat account cannot remove images from the gallery or delete the file.

404.description: File not found or already deleted.

422.description: Invalid file ID format, or `group_id` / `gallery_image_id` missing.

post.description:
Creates a new post on the VRChat group using the server's authenticated VRChat account. Supports group-only or public visibility. The VRChat account must have the appropriate group role.

Requires the `vrchat.post` permission scope on your token.

> *"Sam once posted a meme as a group update. Silvia deleted it. We added a permission check after that."*

text.example: Sam wrote the update. Silvia proofread it.

role_ids.description: Restrict visibility to specific group roles.

image_id.description: VRChat FileID (`file_xxx`) of an image to attach. Obtain one first via `POST /vrchat/image`.

200.description: Post created.

403.description: Missing `vrchat.post` permission scope, or the VRChat account lacks group posting rights.

422.description: Validation failed.

500.description: VRChat API failed to create the post.

post.description:
Schedules a new calendar event on the VRChat group using the server's authenticated VRChat account. The VRChat account must have the appropriate group role. VRChat enforces a limit of 100 events per group per month.

Requires the `vrchat.event` permission scope on your token.

> *"Silvia scheduled a Cozy Cat Night. Sam scheduled a Gaming Marathon. They compromised: Cozy Gaming Night. Silvia knocked Sam's controller off the table 10 minutes in."*

description.example: Join Sam and Silvia for a relaxed hangout. Toys will be knocked off tables.

ends_at.description: Event end time (ISO 8601). Must be after `starts_at`.

role_ids.description: Restrict the event to specific group roles.

200.description: Calendar event created. Silvia has already added it to her nap schedule.

data.title: Sam's Cozy Hangout Night
data.description: Join Sam and Silvia for a relaxed hangout.

403.description: Missing `vrchat.event` permission scope, or the VRChat account lacks group event-creation rights.

422.description: Validation failed — check field formats and that `ends_at` is after `starts_at`.

429.description: VRChat API rate limit reached (max 100 events/month per group).

get.summary: Look up a VRChat member's reputation and group status
get.description:
Returns the group membership status and aggregated reputation tallies for a VRChat user in a given group. Membership data comes from the internal sync (join/leave/ban history), reputation from tracked audit log events.

Requires the `vrchat.reputation` permission scope on your token.

> *"Silvia built the reputation system after Sam kept claiming he'd 'never been warned'. He had been warned four times. The logs don't lie."*

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: The VRChat user ID to look up. Must match the format `usr_<uuid>`.

parameters.name: group_id
parameters.description: The VRChat group ID to scope the reputation lookup to. Must match `grp_<id>` format.

200.description: Reputation retrieved. Silvia printed a copy. Sam looked away.

membership.description: `null` if no membership record exists for this user in the group.

reputation.description: `null` if no audit events have been tracked for this user in the group.

403.description: Missing `vrchat.reputation` permission scope on your token.

example.message: You do not have permission to view VRChat reputation.

404.description: No membership or reputation data found for this user in the specified group. They're a ghost — Silvia checked.

example.message: No data found for this user in the specified group.

422.description: Invalid user ID or missing/invalid group_id. Sam flagged it.

example.message: A valid group_id query parameter is required.

get.description:
Returns a summary of all GitHub security vulnerability alerts tracked from webhook events (`dependabot_alert` and `repository_vulnerability_alert`). Includes total open/fixed/dismissed counts, a per-severity breakdown, and a per-repository breakdown sorted by open count descending.

Silvia reviews these nightly. Sam pretends the critical ones are just decorative.

200.description: Vulnerability summary retrieved successfully.

total_open.description: Number of currently open (unresolved) vulnerability alerts.

total_fixed.description: Total alerts that have been fixed.

total_dismissed.description: Total alerts that have been dismissed or auto-dismissed.

by_severity.description: Open alerts grouped by severity level.

repositories.description: Per-repository breakdown, sorted by open count descending. Silvia's repos always have zero. Sam's are a different story.

by_severity.description: Open alerts by severity for this repository.

post.description:
Receives inbound incident or component-update payloads from an Atlassian Statuspage subscription. The `{code}` path segment identifies the registered source — Silvia checks it against a list of known sources and meows loudly if it is not recognised.

New incident updates are stored and forwarded to configured notification channels (Discord, Telegram). Duplicate deliveries are safely ignored — Silvia never processes the same update twice.

This endpoint requires no authentication token; access is gated solely by the source `{code}`.

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: The unique source code registered for this Statuspage subscription. Sam guards the list — unknown codes get a 404.

requestBody.description: Atlassian Statuspage webhook payload. Must contain either an `incident` or a `component_update` key.

name.example: Sam knocked the auth server off the desk

incident_updates.description: Newest first. The last item is always the initial report.

incident.summary: Incident update — Silvia spotted an outage

incident.name: Sam knocked the auth server off the desk

incident_updates.body: We are investigating the issue — Sam is being gently removed from the server room.

200.description: Webhook received and queued for processing. Sam will process it shortly.

post.description:

get.summary: Look up a Dutch vehicle by license plate
get.description:
Returns vehicle details registered with the Dutch vehicle authority (RDW) for the given license plate (kenteken). Sam looked up Silvia's plate and found three outstanding parking fines. She is not amused.

Data is sourced from the RDW open data API and refreshed nightly. Fuel data is fetched on-demand and cached per vehicle.

Requires the `rdw.lookup` permission scope on your token.

The kenteken is normalised automatically — dashes and spaces are stripped, and it is uppercased before lookup.

parameters.description: Dutch license plate (kenteken). Dashes and spaces are stripped automatically. Silvia's is classified.

post.description:
Receives heartbeat notification payloads from an Uptime Kuma instance (notification type: Webhook). The `{code}` path segment identifies the registered source — Silvia checks it against a list of known sources and will swat away anything she doesn't recognise.

A `down` heartbeat (status `0`) opens an incident for the monitor (or adds an update to the ongoing one); an `up` heartbeat (status `1`) resolves it. Pending (`2`) and maintenance (`3`) heartbeats are ignored — even Sam is allowed a scheduled nap. Duplicate deliveries with the same heartbeat time are safely ignored; Silvia never reports the same hairball twice.

This endpoint requires no authentication token; access is gated solely by the source `{code}`.

requestBody.description: Uptime Kuma webhook payload ('application/json' preset). Must contain both a `heartbeat` and a `monitor` object; the Test button payload (nulls) is acknowledged without processing.

200.description: Webhook received. Returned for valid codes regardless of payload shape, so Uptime Kuma's Test button gets a friendly meow back.
